h: פָּרָשַׁת זָכוֹר, מַאֲמָר ב׳ Parshas Zachor — Maamar Bais

p: "And it shall be, when Hashem your God gives you rest
from all your enemies round about,
you shall erase the memory of Amalek, etc."
"When He gives you rest from all your enemies":
for the chief enemy is the evil inclination,
גַּם אוֹיְבָיו יַשְׁלִים אִתּוֹ [מִשְׁלֵי טז, ז]
"'Even his enemies He will make at peace with him' (Mishlei 16:7) —
this is the evil inclination, etc.";
who is the beginning of kelipah,
And when one overcomes all the kelipos,
one is automatically saved from all the enemies,
שֶׁכֹּחָם רַק עַל יְדֵי כֹּחַ הַקְּלִיפּוֹת
whose power comes only through the power of the kelipos
that enters from them even into the heart of Yisrael,
"in the land which Hashem your God
gives you as an inheritance, etc."
וְהוּא עַל פִּי מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ
This is according to what they said in the Zohar HaKadosh
the time to uproot the dominion, etc.;
'and the voice of the turtledove is heard in our land' —
דְּאַחְסְנוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל עַל יְדָא דִּיהוֹשֻׁעַ וְכוּלֵּי
that Yisrael inherited through Yehoshua, etc."
וְהוּא כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ אַחַר כָּךְ
And it is as they say in the Zohar HaKadosh afterwards:
דְּתוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב אִקְרֵי תּוֹרָה סְתָם וְכוּלֵּי
for Torah she'bichsav is called simply 'Torah,' etc."
דְּתוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה מְקַבֵּל מִתּוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב.
since Torah she'b'al peh receives from Torah she'bichsav —
still, just as the final Hei,
which alludes to Tiferes, in the Name Havayah,
so too "Torah," that is "Tor" followed by Hei,
שֶׁכָּלוּל בָּהּ גַּם הַתּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה.
in which Torah she'b'al peh is also included.
And Torah she'b'al peh is called "HaTor,"
and it receives from the light of Torah she'bichsav.
And this is why the Zohar HaKadosh was precise to say,
to compose a book after Torah she'bichsav.
the portion of each one of Yisrael
as we said in explaining what they said
וְסֵפֶר יְהוֹשֻׁעַ שֶׁעֶרְכָּהּ שֶׁל אֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל הוּא
"and Sefer Yehoshua, for it is the record of Eretz Yisrael"
And Eretz Yisrael is the principal place
for the light of Torah she'b'al peh,
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה זוֹכִין לְנִיצּוּחַ הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע
and through this one merits victory over the evil inclination,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (זֹהַר חֵלֶק א רב, א):
to break the evil inclination except Torah";
drag him to the Beis HaMidrash,"
and there is the place where halachos are newly brought forth
And this is what it says, "in the land, etc.":
דְּאֶרֶץ הוּא בְּחִינַת תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה
for "land" is the aspect of Torah she'b'al peh —
And Shabbos is the day of
"Hashem gives you rest from your sorrow and your agitation"
which is expounded in the Zohar HaKadosh
from the agitation of the evil inclination,
which causes the sorrow and grief.
And then too is a time of bestowal
we call it Torah she'b'al peh";
וְעַל כֵּן שַׁבָּת מְיוּחָד לִמְחִיַּית עֲמָלֵק.
and therefore Shabbos is designated for the eradication of Amalek.
And it is found in the Pesikta
"The Holy One, blessed be He, said:
that I wrote for you in the Torah,
תִּמְחֶה אֶת זֵכֶר עֲמָלֵק [דְּבָרִים כה, יט],
'You shall erase the memory of Amalek' (Devarim 25:19),
זָכוֹר אֵת אֲשֶׁר עָשָׂה לְךָ עֲמָלֵק
These are the two matters of Amalek
that we spoke of (as explained in maamar 1):
that they not rely on their holiness
and should beware of the seductions of the evil inclination,
which can enter even a holy heart,
when they went out of Egypt to receive the Torah,
when they were at a supreme level, as mentioned above;
and also to erase his memory,
the despair he brought into the heart of the stragglers.
And it concludes: "My parable is ashes:
you are the children of Avraham,
who likened himself to ashes, etc."
That is, the kelipah of Amalek is arrogance;
for the roots of the kelipos are
and from them branched out the seventy kelipos,
as is known from the writings of the Arizal;
and Amalek is the beginning of kelipah,
in the manner of what it says:
[יְשַׁעְיָה יד, יד] אֶעֱלֶה עַל בָּמֳתֵי עָב
(Yeshayahu 14:14) "I will ascend above the heights of the clouds;
I will be like the Most High."
"'A man's pride will bring him low' (Mishlei 29:23) —
שֶׁנִּתְגָּאָה עַל הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא וְכוּלֵּי
who exalted himself over the Holy One, blessed be He, etc."
For this came from his arrogance:
that he was not impressed by the greatness of Yisrael
and by the open miracles that occurred then,
to the point that "nations heard and trembled,"
yet he, out of his arrogance,
And Avraham Avinu, peace be upon him,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁנִּרְמָז בְּמַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר [בְּרֵאשִׁית כד, א]
as is hinted in what it says (Bereishis 24:1),
וְזֶה סוֹד מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ (בָּבָא מְצִיעָא פז, א):
and this is the secret of what they said (Bava Metzia 87a):
"Until Avraham there was no old age"
And this he merited through humility,
for he likened himself to ashes;
"hidden of all hidden, which is called Ayin"
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב זֹהַר חֵלֶק ב סד, ב).
שֶׁכְּנֶגֶד קְדוּשַּׁת אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
which corresponds to the holiness of Avraham Avinu, peace be upon him,
and to the aspect of Atika
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב תִּקּוּנֵי זֹהַר תִּקּוּן יח לד, א),
for the holiness of the Shabbos prayers
is like the holiness of the meals —
so that through mentioning his name below
we will merit the eradication of Amalek,
וְלִזְכּוֹת לִקְדוּשַּׁת אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
and merit the holiness of Avraham Avinu, peace be upon him,
for he likened himself to ashes, as mentioned above.
And through this we are redeemed.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: R. Yehudah Aryeh Leib Alter, Sefas Emes, Shabbos Zachor 5638, s.v. Od yisba'er — “The Sages established this at the end of the year, and Haman’s fall likewise occurred in Adar, on the basis of ‘When He gives you rest from all your enemies round about.’ After the surrounding forces of impurity have been burned away, Amalek’s name can be erased. What occurred in the course of Israel’s history also occurs every year; therefore, at the year’s end, ‘when He gives you rest from all your enemies,’ there is an erasure of Amalek.”

paragraphs.text: Connection: Sefas Emes reads the same condition as an inward sequence: release from the surrounding forces prepares the attack on Amalek itself. He then applies that sequence to the annual calendar, explaining how the Torah’s national condition can also inform the present observance of Zachor.

paragraphs.text: Zohar III, Vayikra 4b — “'The time of pruning has arrived'—the time to uproot the dominion of the rulers of the nations, so that they should not rule over Israel, when the Mishkan was established. 'The voice of the turtledove is heard in our land'—this is the lower land that Israel inherited through Yehoshua. What is the voice of the turtledove? It is the supernal guide who joined her when Shlomo built the Temple below. ... In the Book of Aggadah it says: 'The voice of the tor' is the Oral Torah. The Written Torah is called Torah without qualification; the Oral Torah is called tor, as with vayiker and vayikra: one is complete and the other is not so.” The Zohar supplies both the literal inheritance through Yehoshua and the interpretation of tor as Oral Torah. Rav Tzadok develops their conjunction into the meaning of the land as each Jew's share in Oral Torah.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Purim Katan 2 — “Menasheh… is the time of erasing Amalek, who is the evil inclination; and from Efrayim came Yehoshua, who bequeathed Eretz Yisrael to Yisrael, which is the root of the holiness of Torah she’b’al peh.” There Rav Tzadok reads the two halves of Adar in a leap year as these two forces, so the war on Amalek is paired with Yehoshua’s inheritance of Torah she’b’al peh, as in the two conditions of the pasuk here.

paragraphs.text: Zohar I, Mikeitz 202a — “We learned: A person should always rouse the good inclination against the evil inclination and strive against it. If it departs from him, well; if not, he should occupy himself with Torah, for there is nothing that breaks the evil inclination except Torah. If it departs, good; if not, let him remind it of the day of death in order to break it.” The Zohar gives a sequence of active resistance, Torah and remembrance of death. Rav Tzadok emphasizes the Oral Torah's lived study as the means of transforming the inward enemy.

paragraphs.text: Sukkah 52b — “The school of Rabbi Yishmael taught: If this repulsive one encounters you, draw him to the study hall. If he is stone, he will dissolve; if iron, he will shatter. If stone, he dissolves, for it says, 'All who are thirsty, go to water,' and 'Water wears away stones.' If iron, he shatters, for it says, 'Is not My word like fire, says Hashem, and like a hammer that shatters rock?'” The source's remedy is study in the beis midrash. Rav Tzadok identifies this setting particularly with the active development of Oral Torah, rather than treating knowledge as merely an intellectual possession.

paragraphs.text: Midrash Tanchuma, Ki Seitzei 5 — “The Holy One, blessed be He, said to Israel: 'Be careful concerning those two remembrances I wrote for you in Torah: Blot out Amalek's remembrance; remember what Amalek did to you.' 'Proverbs of ashes': If you merit, you are the children of Avraham, who compared himself to ashes, saying, 'I am dust and ashes.' If not, 'your defenses are defenses of clay': prepare yourselves for the servitude of Egypt, as it says, 'They embittered their lives with hard labor.' Another reading: for the servitude of kingdoms, as it says, 'Plowers plowed upon my back.'” The Midrash links both remembering and erasure to Avraham's ashes and to deliverance from servitude. Rav Tzadok explains that humility counters Amalek's pride and that the two commands address the two dangers distinguished in Maamar 1. The same formulation was not independently located in the checked Pesikta 12transcription.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Sefer Sod HaNachash, attributed to Rabbi Yosef Gikatilla, opening, pp.30–32 — “Avraham, the mystery of the right arm, has thirty-five princes attached through Yishmael; beside him is Egypt, second to the Land of Israel. ... Know that on the left is Yitzchak, and thirty-five princes attach to him through Esav. All those princes are generally called nations, and the first of them all is Amalek, descendant of Esav.” The edition attributes this treatise to Gikatilla. That attribution has not been independently established from a manuscript. Its Hebrew reads ben Esav in the broad sense of Esav's descendant; Amalek is his grandson. This passage explicitly gives the thirty-five princes on each side and their attachment through Yishmael and Esav. It corroborates the division. Megaleh Amukot on Lech Lecha, as reported by Shem MiShmuel, Mattos, gives the same scheme in the Lurianic school: “The prince of Yishmael has under him thirty-five princes on the right, and the prince of Esav thirty-five princes on the left; these are the seventy princes of the nations.” A passage in the Arizal's own transmitted writings stating the division has not been located.

paragraphs.text: Bamidbar Rabbah 13:3 — “'A person's pride will bring him low'—this is Amalek, who exalted himself against the Holy One with insults and blasphemies. He directed the zemorah toward Him, taking Israel's circumcised members and throwing them upward, insulting and blaspheming and saying, 'Is this what You desired?' Thus, 'He struck at your rear'—a blow at the tail. 'The lowly of spirit will attain honor'—this is Yehoshua, who killed him, as it says, 'Yehoshua weakened Amalek and his people.'” The source explicitly identifies the spiritual fault as pride and contrasts it with Yehoshua's lowliness. Rav Tzadok relates Avraham's self-description as ashes to the same opposing quality of humility.

paragraphs.text: Bava Metzia 87a — “Until Avraham there was no old age. One wishing to speak with Avraham would speak with Yitzchak; one wishing to speak with Yitzchak would speak with Avraham. Avraham came and asked for mercy, and old age came to be, as it says, 'Avraham was old, advanced in days.'” The Gemara explains the visible distinction of old age between father and son. Rav Tzadok reads this manifestation as the outward sign of Avraham's attainment of Atika; that mystical identification is his further interpretation.

paragraphs.text: Tikkunei Zohar, Tikkun 18, 34a — “There are three prayers on Shabbos, with Musaf as a fourth. The evening prayer, 'You sanctified,' is the lower Shechinah, from the left side, where the Leviim are, of whom it says, 'Sanctify the Leviim.' The morning prayer, 'Moshe rejoices in the gift of his portion,' is the soul of every living being, the supernal Mother. ... The third prayer, 'You are One and Your name is One,' is the Divine Name, the middle pillar, which unites with both.” The checked passage assigns the Shabbos prayers to distinct supernal aspects. It expressly calls Shacharis the supernal Mother; it does not explicitly name Atika in these lines. Rav Tzadok's identification of prayer with the corresponding meal and Avraham's holiness is the further interpretation developed in the manuscript.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Bnei Yissaschar, Adar 3:3 — “Be the children of Avraham — he was the first to wage war on the kelipah of Amalek… and he likened himself to dust, nullified to His will.” Expounding the same midrash, the Bnei Yissaschar likewise sets Avraham against Amalek, noting that “ram” (haughty) equals Amalek in gematria and that Avraham’s “dust and ashes” is the self-nullification that undoes Amalek’s pride.
